findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at class-definition (import) time, so every instance created without an explicit `queued` gets the same stale timestamp from when the module was first imported (e.g. worker process start), not the time the assignment was queued. Since this PR's stated purpose is to use `queued` as context for breaking sync cycles, any logic relying on it being accurate will be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Task passes new assignment_source kwarg to provider sync_assignee_outbound implementations that don't accept it
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. The abstract method in IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound (mixins/issues.py line 397) was NOT updated to include `assignment_source` — only sync_status_outbound was — and none of the provider implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) are changed in this PR. Any provider implementation whose signature doesn't accept `assignment_source` will raise TypeError at runtime, breaking assignee outbound sync entirely for those integrations. The abstract signature and all implementations must be updated (or the kwarg not forwarded).

findings.title: from_dict does not deserialize the queued datetime
findings.body: `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` directly. After a round trip through the Celery task (to_dict → JSON kwargs → from_dict), the `queued` value arrives as an ISO string, so the reconstructed AssignmentSource has `queued: str` instead of `datetime`. Any downstream code that formats, compares, or does arithmetic on `queued` will fail or behave incorrectly. `to_dict` should serialize to an ISO string explicitly and `from_dict` should parse it back with `datetime.fromisoformat` (or `parse`), and `from_dict` should also not silently swallow a string that fails later.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound gained an assignment_source parameter that is never propagated or used
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature was changed to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no caller in this PR passes it and no provider implementation is shown being updated to use it. This is dead API surface that will drift from actual provider implementations (which still have the old signature), and misleads readers into thinking status outbound sync is also cycle-protected when it is not. Either wire it through the status outbound path or drop the parameter.

findings.title: No test covering cross-integration propagation or inbound-triggered cycle break
findings.body: The new test only verifies that the same integration is skipped when AssignmentSource is passed explicitly. There is no end-to-end test of the actual scenario the PR fixes: an inbound webhook (sync_group_assignee_inbound) producing an assignment_source that suppresses outbound sync back to the originating integration, and — critically — that outbound sync still fires for a *different* linked integration (the code comment in should_sync promises this). A regression in the comparison logic (e.g. suppressing all integrations, or none) would not be caught.
